Request for approval of exterior modifications, landscaping, and new signage for the Cruz-n-Shine Car Wash located at 159 Maple Avenue W, Docket No. PF-54-20-BAR, in the C-2 General Commercial zoning district; filed by Matthew Hawkins, Helbing Lipp Recny Architects, Inc., project architect.

Mr. John Recny was present to represent the application.  Mr. Recny stated they were back to address the three items the Board deferred at a previous meeting.  The first item: the lumens for the sign were recalculated and the sign is now at 94 lumens.  The second item, new samples of the carbine red and zinc yellow that will be on the façade were brought to town hall for the Board to view.  The third item, the acrylic pole sign, will be white acrylic with a translucent red and yellow acrylic for the red and yellow parts of the sign.  

Mr. Cheselka asked what the lumen and kelvins were for the pole sign.  Mr. Recny stated they were the same as what they had been previously as they are not changing the lights in the sign.  The recessed lights were also inquired about as well in reference to the light spread.  

Mr. Layer stated the pewter color was more brown, than gray, but felt it would go better with the scheme.  Mr. Layer asked about the yellow color on the sign and building as they seem to differ.  Mr. Recny stated they were trying to get them to as close as possible in color.   

Mr. Layer made a motion the application be approved as submitted.  

Ms. Hanley asked for discussion as a portion of the application had been approved at a prior meeting and wanted to know if the motion should encapsulate what had been approved previously.  Mr. Cheselka stated he understood that it was the new items from the original that they were reviewing.  Ms. Hanley wanted to make sure all items were being presented and approved.  Ms. West stated that the whole package was presented and could be approved as the complete package that evening.  

Motion to approve: Mr.  Layer
Second: Mr. Cheselka
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Chesleka, and Ms. Hanley
EventItemTitle: 159 Maple Ave W - Cruz ‘n’ Shine Car Wash - Sign and Exterior Modification

EventItemActionText:
Request for approval of new signage for the T-Mobile located at 256 Maple Ave E Docket No. PF-53-20-BAR, in the C-1A Special Commercial zoning district; filed by Valeria Nitzey, Shane’s Signs, project agent.

Ms. Valeria Nitzey and Shane Nitzey were present to represent the application.

Ms. West told the Board members the lumens for the sign had been clarified would be 69 total lumens.  

Mr. Layer if the channel letters were considered slim line, Mr. Nitzey asked for clarification. Mr. Layer stated the lighting and box used when originally approved was a slim box with a small projection beyond the surface of the building.  Mr. Layer stated, he wanted to confirm that it was similar to the other signage.  Mr. Nitzey stated it was a slim / shallow depth letter.

Ms. Hanley asked if color of the letter would be the same as the current sign.  Mr. Nitzey stated only 2 acrylic whites are used in signs, 2447: one is milky and slightly darker, and the other. 7328:  is a lighter color.  The 2447 was created to work with LED’s and is more translucent than the 7328.  Mr. Nitzey stated that the use of white faces with LED’s it should be made out of 2447 industry wide.      

Motion to approve with the change in lumens from 6500 to 69.1 lumens: Mr. Cheselka
Second: Mr. Layer
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Cheselka, and Ms. Hanley

Request for approval of signage for the SunTrust/BB&T Bank located at 515 Maple Ave E Docket No. PF-55-20-BAR in the C-1 Local Commercial zoning district; filed by Gary Brent, MG Permits LLC, project agent.

Mr. Gary Brent was present to represent the application.  Mr. Brent stated that the application mentioned the existing pylon was to be removed or replaced which was incorrect.  The pylon sign was only to be refaced.  The existing sign is to just be refaced with the aluminum face with push through acrylic letters.  No internal lighting, structure, or cabinet changes will be made, jut the panel.  The window signage will be the same, reface of digitally printed, white graphic. applied vinyl.

Ms. Hanley asked Ms. West if the completed application had all the correct information and if the discrepancies were only in the supporting documentation.  Ms. West stated that was correct and mentioned that the Board could require updated documents.  Ms. Hanley stated the Board could defer to the application.

Mr. Layer asked for confirmation that the pylon sign was aluminum with punch letters, Mr. Brent stated that was correct. 

Ms. Hanley asked if there was a wrap around the pylon sign.  Mr. Brent stated that the existing sign size will remain including the face of the sign. 

Mr. Cheselka asked if the lighting would remain the same for the pylon sign.  Mr. Brent stated it would remain the same.

Mr. Brent mentioned to the Board that these signs, although permanent signs would be temporary in nature as Suntrust/BB&T would change to their new name over the next year or so.  There was additional conversation regarding the possibilities for signs in the future.

Motion to approve with the proviso that the approval is for the written application and not the supporting documentation: Ms. Hanley
Second: Mr. Layer
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Cheselka, and Ms. Hanley
EventItemTitle: 515 Maple Ave E - SunTrust/BB&T Bank - Sign

Request for approval of exterior modifications for Westwood Country Club, located at 800 Maple Ave E, Docket No. PF-58-20-BAR in the RS-16 Single-Family Detached Residential zoning district; filed by Braden Field, MTFA Architecture, project architect.

Mr. Braden Field was present to represent the application of the 1 story addition, to the main clubhouse, of a fitness area and cart maintenance/storage facility.  The cart maintenance / storage facility is partially built into grade making it partially concealed from the upper level of the parking lot.  It is primarily visible from the lower level.  There will also be an accessible roof terrace area as extension of the second level of the clubhouse.  There is finished paver material, railing, trellis, stand-alone open air roof to provide shading and architectural character. 

Mr. Cheselka asked about why there were three scuppers on the right side, but not all the way across.  Mr. Field stated they did not want scuppers over the paved area as they are for over flow drainage.  There will be secondary over flow drains below the pavers.  

Motion to approve: Mr. Cheselka
Second: Ms. Layer
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Cheselka, and Ms. Hanley
EventItemTitle: 800 Maple Ave E - Westwood Country Club - Exterior Modifications

EventItemActionText:
Request for approval of a repair and replacement of a retaining wall at 100 East Street SE, Docket No. PF-64-20-BAR, in the C-1/T Local Commercial / Transitional zoning districts; filed by Stephen Kenney, RV Architects, project architect.

Mr. Stephen Kenney was present to represent the application.  Mr. Kenney stated this was an emergency repair to the retaining wall on the east side of the property.  There fallen portion is between the office building and the town homes which is about 900-100 feet long.  Mr. Kenney explained what they believed caused the collapse and then stated they proposed quick brick which is a concrete brick with coloring to give the look of brick.  They will be able to install two courses of quick brick versus the 3 courses of regular nominal brick.  There will be a transition back to real brick at the cap and the proffers require a 6 foot masonry wall.  Some of the grading will be fixed to include adding a swale which will handle the drainage better.  Mr. Kenney stated they are also proposing shrubs rather than trees to allow sun in the rear yards of the town homes.   

Mr. Layer asked if there would be a pattern in the new brick, Mr. Kenney stated there would be a running bond.  Mr. Layer asked if there would be two different colors.  Mr. Kenney stated there would be a built in flashing and it would mimic the existing brick.  Mr. Layer asked about the landscape, Mr. Kenney stated the new planting was on the far left side and what was “X” out on the right was cut down for safety purposes.  Mr. Layer stated the legend showed proposed trees and proposed shrubs.  Mr. Kenney stated that the legend was created before the HOA stated they did not want trees.  

Ms. Hanley asked if there would be weep holes in the new wall, Mr. Kenney stated they would be adding weep holes to relieve the water pressure.  They would install 2 inch diameter pipe at the low side and backed up with gravel and filter fabric.  Ms. Hanley asked if any drainage tile would be added.  Mr. Kenney stated they would put in drain tile as well as tap into what was already there.  Ms. Hanley asked if the walls would be joined with mortar.  Mr. Kenney stated that was correct unless the structural engineer encouraged and expansion joint.  

Mr. Cheselka asked if the cap would run with single brick perpendicular across the top.  Mr. Kenney stated it would be a soldier course and header course to mimic what was already there.  

Ms. van Doorn asked the reason for using quick brick rather than regular nominal brick.  Mr. Kenney stated it was a cost issue, but also that structurally, 2 bricks with rebar in between does not allow enough space for the right amount of mortar.  With the quick brick the rebar can be run down the core and get good bonding with the mortar.  

Mr. Baldwin asked about the Home Owners Association, Mr. Kenney stated they had a letter stating the HOA is in agreeance with the changes.  Mr. Baldwin asked what the difference would be between the new and existing brick.  Mr. Kenney pointed out the photo that would show the difference.  He continued stating most people will not be able to notice the difference between the new and old brick.

Ms. Susan Forbes, of 113 Follin Ln SE, spoke stating she and three other neighbors back to the wall and stated that the neighbor on the Maple St. side may not want trees, but the other neighbors would like them for privacy.   Mr. Kenney stated they would be open to adding trees.  There was continued discussion between the applicant and the resident regarding the trees and shrubs.  

Mr. Cheselka asked if the HOA Board was in agreeance with the trees.  Ms. Forbes stated it was an informal discussion in their yards.  

Mr. Baldwin asked why Ms. Forbes could not plant trees on her side of the wall.  Ms. Forbes said she would have some trees, but they wouldn’t be as high or give as much privacy.  Ms. Forbes stated that they would like to see the quick brick approved and thought that all the neighbors would want a mix of the shrubs and trees.  

Ms. Hanley asked which lot Ms. Forbes home was located; Ms. Forbes said she was on lot 8. Ms. Hanley stated she asked to see what trees could possibly be planted although the owner of the commercial building was well with in their required tree canopy coverage.  There was continued discussion regarding trees.  

Mr. Baldwin asked Mr. Kenney his thoughts of approving the wall and deferring the landscaping.  Mr. Kenney asked if there was a way to have a chairman’s review for the landscaping.  Ms. West stated it would have to come back for a full meeting.  Ms. Hanley suggested the Board approve three understory trees at 20-30 feet high at maturity.  Mr. Kenney stated Mr. Meruvia would be willing to work with homeowners regarding the trees.  Ms. West recommended the approval be conditioned with the trees are from the official town list.  

Ms. van Doorn inquired who would absorb the cost of the wall, Mr. Kenney stated it would be the property owner.  Ms. van Doorn asked if trees on the Town of Vienna approved list would not be suitable, would the owner be required to choose those trees.   Ms. West stated that through site work if it is discovered that a tree is not appropriate the applicant can come back and ask for a revision.  Mr. Layer stated they could move forward if a decision / agreement could be made regarding the allowable appropriate trees by the town and number of trees.  Mr. Baldwin stated the Board may need to defer the landscaping portion of the application.  Ms. Hanley stated she didn’t want to defer as what was presented is acceptable and any changes would need to come from the applicant.  Mr. Kenney stated they could put in three trees with smaller root bases around lots 7 and 8.  Mr. Layer stated he was okay with either direction.  There was continued discussion regarding the trees.  Mr. Baldwin asked for a motion.

Mr. Layer split the motion in to two.  The first motion was to approve the repair and replacement of the retaining wall as submitted.  Ms. Hanley seconded. 

Motion to approve the retaining wall as submitted: Mr. Layer
Second: Ms. Hanley
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Cheselka, and Ms. Hanley

Mr. Layer made a motion to approve the landscaping with the condition that the trees are from a selection of the Town of Vienna approved tree list and found appropriate for that installation.  There will need to be three trees planted in addition to the shrubs already shown on the plan and coordinated with the adjacent property owners.  If the number or conditions stated change, it will require a separate motion at a different time. 

Ms. van Doorn asked if there would be adequate space for the trees replacing the shrubs.  Mr. Kenney stated they would need to reduce the amount of shrubs.  Mr. Layer asked about amending the motion to include that information.  
 

Motion to approve the landscaping with the following conditions: Mr. Layer
	-trees are from an appropriate selection from the Town of Vienna tree list
	-trees are appropriate for that type of installation
	-the trees planted in addition to the shrubs shown in the plan
	-coordination with the adjacent property owners regarding the trees
	-shrubs will be altered to accommodate additional trees
-if the number or conditions stated change, it will require a separate motion at a different time.
Second: Ms. Hanley
Approved: 5-0
Ayes: Ms. van Doorn, Mr. Layer, Mr. Baldwin, Mr. Cheselka, and Ms. Hanley
EventItemTitle: 100 East St SE - Repair and Replacement of Retaining Wall
